clinicalPearls: The most common congenital tumour of the newborn, arising at the base of the coccyx and typically presenting as a large sacral mass, more often in females
The Altman classification describes the balance of external versus internal (presacral/pelvic) tumour, which affects detectability and surgical difficulty
Predominantly external tumours are usually recognised at birth, whereas mainly internal lesions may present later with pelvic mass effect, constipation, or urinary symptoms
Most tumours found in the neonatal period are benign (mature or immature teratoma), but the risk of malignancy rises the later the lesion presents
Serum alpha-fetoprotein is a useful marker; persistently elevated or rising levels after resection raise concern for malignant (yolk sac) elements or recurrence
Large vascular tumours detected antenatally can cause high-output cardiac failure and fetal hydrops due to arteriovenous shunting
Definitive treatment is complete surgical excision including the coccyx, since leaving the coccyx behind markedly increases recurrence
Long-term follow-up with clinical review and tumour markers is required to detect recurrence and to monitor bowel and bladder function
reference.pathophysiology: Sacrococcygeal teratoma is a germ cell tumour thought to arise from pluripotent cells near the primitive streak (Hensen's node) at the caudal end of the embryo. It therefore contains tissues derived from multiple germ layers and grows at the coccygeal region, extending externally, into the pelvis, or both. Large, highly vascular tumours can act as arteriovenous shunts, causing high-output heart failure and hydrops in the fetus. Malignant transformation, usually to yolk sac tumour, becomes more likely with delayed diagnosis and with predominantly internal, poorly detected lesions.
additionalDifferentials: Myelomeningocele or other neural tube defect
additionalInvestigations: Antenatal and postnatal ultrasound to assess size, vascularity, and internal extent
MRI of the pelvis and spine to define intrapelvic extension and exclude a spinal component
Serum alpha-fetoprotein at baseline and during follow-up
Fetal echocardiography and monitoring for hydrops in large vascular antenatal lesions
Histological examination of the resected specimen to grade maturity and detect malignant elements
redFlags: Antenatal high-output cardiac failure or hydrops from a large vascular tumour, which is life-threatening
Rapid tumour growth or haemorrhage requiring urgent surgical planning
Rising alpha-fetoprotein after resection suggesting malignant recurrence
Delayed presentation of an internal tumour, which carries higher malignancy risk
reference.prognosis: Benign lesions completely excised in the neonatal period with removal of the coccyx have an excellent prognosis. Prognosis worsens with malignant histology, incomplete excision, delayed diagnosis, and antenatal complications such as hydrops. Even after benign resection, some children have long-term bowel or bladder dysfunction.
pitfalls: Failing to remove the coccyx, which greatly increases recurrence risk
Missing a predominantly internal (presacral) tumour on external examination alone
Neglecting postoperative alpha-fetoprotein surveillance for recurrence
Overlooking associated anorectal or spinal anomalies and later functional problems
references: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
management: Complete surgical excision of the tumour with en bloc removal of the coccyx as the definitive treatment, reducing recurrence risk
Platinum-based chemotherapy (such as cisplatin, etoposide and bleomycin) for malignant yolk sac elements or unresectable and metastatic disease
Antenatal foetal surveillance with serial ultrasound and foetal echocardiography, considering early delivery or foetal intervention for large vascular lesions causing high-output failure or hydrops
Serial serum alpha-fetoprotein monitoring after resection to detect malignant transformation or recurrence
Histological grading of the resected specimen to assess maturity and identify malignant components guiding adjuvant therapy
Long-term surveillance for functional sequelae such as bowel and bladder dysfunction after pelvic resection
Coordinated care through a paediatric surgical, oncology and neonatology multidisciplinary team
